title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-06-24
source: Aud > cassette x 2 > CD, mics balcony center 15' spread

ai_review.summary: A legendary audience tape of one of the Dead’s all‑time great shows, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and flawless, psychedelic transitions.
ai_review.review: Listeners rave about this June 1970 performance as a near‑mythic moment in Dead history – the band weaves together Dark Star, Not Fade Away, Sugar Magnolia and several deep cuts with telepathic interplay.  The audience recording is surprisingly clear and captures the crowd’s excitement, though occasional drop‑outs and a busted string keep it from being perfect.

ai_rating.rationale: Over twenty enthusiastic reviews praise both the musical performance (standout jams, seamless transitions) and the audio quality; only minor technical complaints are noted, resulting in an overall near‑exceptional rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and lively, captures crowd excitement well; a few reviewers note occasional drop‑outs, a busted string, and minor mix quirks that keep it from being flawless.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for its seamless, psychedelic transitions – dark jams flow into Sugar Magnolia, NFA launches a cascade of improvisations, and the band constantly chases each other around the stage.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is described as incendiary, blazing, and almost other‑worldly throughout the performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is noted for locking in with the drums and feeding the tight chase dynamics during NFA.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir receives kudos for his vocal grit and guitar on tracks like Me & My Uncle, embodying an outlaw‑cowboy vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum lock is repeatedly praised; the rhythm section is called ‘locked’ and drives the show’s momentum.
